faqs.q: What are finned U-bend tubes used for?
faqs.a: Finned U-bend tubes are finned tubes bent into a U for compact air-cooled and heat-recovery coils. The fins are stripped from the bend, which is formed on a bare section after finning, so the fins are not crushed or torn.

faqs.q: How are finned U-bend tubes made without damaging the fins?
faqs.a: The legs are finned first and the bend is then formed on a section of tube left bare, so the bend can be checked for wall thinning and ovality like any other U-tube. Leg lengths and bend radii follow your bend schedule.

faqs.q: What sizes do finned U-bend tubes come in?
faqs.a: Finned U-bend tubes are made to order, with sizes confirmed with the quotation rather than listed in a table. Send the base tube grade, OD and wall, the fin height, thickness and pitch, the finned and bare lengths and the bend schedule.

faqs.q: Which fin types and base tube materials suit finned U-bend tubes?
faqs.a: Wound, embedded or extruded fins can be put on the straight legs, chosen for the duty and temperature. Base tube is carbon steel, stainless steel, copper or copper alloy, to the standard on the order. Integral low-fin U-bends are listed separately.

faqs.q: What is the difference between finned U-bend tubes and low-fin U-bend tubes?
faqs.a: Finned U-bends carry applied fins (wound, embedded or extruded) on the legs, while the [low-fin U-bend tubes](/p/low-fin-u-bend-tubes) have integral fins rolled from the tube wall with a plain land at each tangent. Low-fin gives extra shell-side surface in a removable bundle.

faqs.q: What bend radius and leg length can finned U-bend tubes have?
faqs.a: Bend radius is to your bend schedule: you give the centreline radius and leg length for each row. The bend is formed on a bare length, so the finned length and the bare length at each end are both stated on the order.

faqs.q: What tests are done on finned U-bend tubes?
faqs.a: The fin bond and fin pitch are checked along the length, and the base tube is tested to its own standard. A mill test certificate to EN 10204 3.1 is available on request, and third-party inspection can be arranged against your inspection and test plan.

faqs.q: Can finned U-bend tubes replace existing tubes in a bundle?
faqs.a: Yes. Send the old drawing or a sample length and we measure the base tube and the fin before we quote, so the new tubes fit the existing bundle and tube supports. Fin pitch and bare lengths are matched at the same time.

faqs.q: Where are finned U-bend tubes used?
faqs.a: Finned U-bend tubes are used in compact air-cooled and heat-recovery coils. Fin type on the legs follows the duty and temperature; our [finned tubes shelf](/c/finned-tubes) and [types of finned tubes guide](/blog/types-of-finned-tubes) help you compare options.

faqs.q: What information does a finned U-bend tube enquiry need?
faqs.a: Send the base tube standard, grade, OD and wall; fin type, material, height, thickness and fins per inch; finned length and bare length at each end; the bend schedule; quantity; any heat treatment of the bends; and your inspection and certificate requirements.

faqs.q: Is the Finned U-Bend Tubes available from Indus Hydraulics in Dubai, and what is the lead time?
faqs.a: The Finned U-Bend Tubes is built to order and supplied from Dubai, UAE, with shipping worldwide. The lead time is confirmed on the quotation. Send the size, rating and quantity through [our contact page](/contact) and we confirm the build and delivery date.

faqs.q: What is the U-bend wall thinning rule for finned U-bends?
faqs.a: Wall thinning and ovality at the bend are checked like any other U-tube, to the specification on your order. Our [U-bend wall thinning and bend radius guide](/blog/u-bend-tubes-bend-radius-wall-thinning) explains how the figures are worked out.

faqs.q: What are low-fin U-bend tubes used for?
faqs.a: Low-fin U-bend tubes are integral low-fin tubes bent into U-tubes for removable shell-and-tube bundles. The fins are removed at the bend, leaving a plain land at each tangent, so the bundle gets the extra shell-side surface of low-fin tube. Used in gas-plant U-tube exchangers.

faqs.q: How do I read the low-fin U-bend part number IH-TF-UF-LOF-0254-211-H012?
faqs.a: IH-TF-UF-LOF-0254-211-H012 is the 1 in (25.4 mm) low-fin U-bend row, and IH-TF-UF-LOF-0190-211-H012 is the 3/4 in (19.05 mm) row. The 0190 and 0254 blocks are the OD in tenths of a millimetre, and both rows use a 2.108 mm wall at 26 FPI.

faqs.q: What sizes do low-fin U-bend tubes come in?
faqs.a: The size table lists 2 sizes, 3/4 in (19.05 mm) and 1 in (25.4 mm) OD, both with a 2.108 mm wall, 26 fins per inch (1024 fins per metre) and a 1.245 mm fin height. Other sizes are made on request.

faqs.q: What is the fin geometry on low-fin U-bend tubes?
faqs.a: The 26 FPI fin is 1.245 mm high, with root diameter 16.561 mm on the 3/4 in tube and 22.911 mm on the 1 in tube, and 1.651 mm wall under the fin. The fin tips are no larger than the plain-end OD, so the tube passes through standard tube-sheet holes.

faqs.q: How tight a bend radius can low-fin U-bend tubes have?
faqs.a: A centreline radius of 1.5×OD is available, with dimensional tolerances guaranteed from 2×OD. The land at the bend tangent is ±6.35 mm, and the plain-end length tolerance on U-bends is +12.7 / −0 mm.

faqs.q: What materials are low-fin U-bend tubes made from?
faqs.a: Tube material is SA-334 Gr 6, SA-179, stainless or Cu-Ni, with the fin integral (rolled from the tube wall). Carbon steel grades offered at 26 FPI are SA-179, SA-214 and SA-334 Gr 1, 3 and 6.

faqs.q: Which standards apply to low-fin U-bend tubes?
faqs.a: The listing cites ASTM A498, ASTM A1012 and ASTM B359, with ASME SA334 Gr 6 for the low-temperature carbon steel option. Equivalent grades in other standards are indicative only, and we check them against each tender.

faqs.q: What tests are done on low-fin U-bend tubes?
faqs.a: Eddy current testing is done after finning and every U-bend is hydrotested after bending. A mill test certificate to EN 10204 3.1 is available on request, and third-party inspection can be arranged.

faqs.q: Low-fin U-bend tubes or plain U-bends: which is right for a gas-plant exchanger?
faqs.a: Choose low-fin when the shell side limits the duty, because the fins add outside surface without changing the OD. Use plain tube for fouling service. Our [finned U-bend tubes](/p/finned-u-bend-tubes) are the alternative with applied fins, and the [low-fin tube retubing guide](/blog/integral-low-fin-tubes-condenser-retubing) explains the swap.

faqs.q: Where are low-fin U-bend tubes used?
faqs.a: They are used in U-tube exchangers in gas plants, including low-temperature service in SA-334 Gr 6. Typical size is 19.05–25.4 mm OD, and the bundle can still be removed for shell-side cleaning.

faqs.q: Can I get low-fin U-bend tubes from Dubai?
faqs.a: We supply low-fin U-bend tubes from Dubai, UAE and ship worldwide with the best lead times. The two listed rows are typical sizes and other sizes are made on request; send the bend schedule, grade and quantity through [our contact page](/contact).

faqs.q: What bend schedule do I send for low-fin U-bend tubes?
faqs.a: Send the centreline radius and leg length for each row, the base tube standard and grade, OD and wall, quantity, and any heat treatment of the bends. We quote with the mill certificates and inspection you need.
